verdict.reason: Both provide feasible six-month plans within the $8,000 monthly budget, correctly calculate gross profit and advertising acquisition economics, and investigate whether existing contracts are also threatened. A immediately funds the projected four-win replacement rate; B stages spending while testing referrals and advertising. Both condition expansion on observed economics and delivery capacity, making either approach defensible.

Both defensibly choose B based on relevant experience while making procurement, technical feasibility, and sustainable economics explicit tests. Both account for limited savings and propose useful historical validation without promising measurable failure prevention within six months. A allows more procurement flexibility and explores partners; B demands earlier financial commitment. These are defensible tradeoffs given the unspecified purchase timelines.

Both recommend a focused, paid veterinary note-writing experiment, appropriately distinguish one clinic's usage from repeatable demand, and provide concrete eight-week milestones. Runway arithmetic is reasonable. B specifies stronger retention criteria and founder responsibilities; A explicitly addresses different responses to payment versus usage failures. Neither has a material substantive advantage.
